title: Deposit Percentages by Combined Disability Rating — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery Reinstatement Schedule
content:
A debtor reinstating a cancelled repayment plan on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** pays a reduced share of the deposit according to the combined rating of a running **Disability Compensation** award and the age of the debt notice.

## Schedule

| Combined rating on the running Disability Compensation award | Debt notice no older than the waiver window | Deposit percentage |
|---|---|---|
| 60 percent or more | Yes | 55 percent (high-rating deposit percentage) |
| 30 to 50 percent | Yes | 80 percent (mid-rating deposit percentage) |
| Any rating, or no running award | No | No reduced percentage under this schedule |
| Below 30 percent, or no running award | Either | No reduced percentage under this schedule |

The reinstatement deposit is taken at the percentage the schedule gives.

**The waiver window**, in calendar days from the notice date to the day of the payment, is the debt type's:

| Debt type | Waiver window (calendar days after the notice) |
|---|---|
| Education Overpayment (Chapters 30, 35 and 1606) | 180 |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill Housing and Books Overpayment | 180 |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill Tuition and Fees Overpayment | 180 |
| Disability Compensation Overpayment | 180 |
| Veterans Pension Overpayment | 180 |
| Home Loan Guaranty Debt | 365 |

A notice exactly on the last day of the window (180 or 365 days old) is still within it.

## Hypothetical cases

- A 70 percent award, notice 120 days old on a Disability Compensation Overpayment: a deposit figure of 400.00 USD is taken at 55 percent, 220.00 USD.
- A 40 percent award, notice 180 days old on a Veterans Pension Overpayment: taken at 80 percent.
- A 40 percent award, notice 181 days old on the same type: no reduced percentage under this schedule.
- A 90 percent award, notice 300 days old on a Home Loan Guaranty Debt: within its 365-day window, taken at 55 percent.
